title: Canada Reminds International Students: You Can Work Only If Your Study Permit Says So
excerpt: IRCC's fresh warning: the permission is printed on the permit itself, off-campus work is capped at 24 hours a week in session, and breaching the conditions can cost a student their status.
body:
• Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has reminded international students that they can work in Canada only if the conditions printed on their study permit say they can — a permit alone does not authorise a job.
  • Students eligible for off-campus work may work up to 24 hours per week while classes are in session.
  • Working more than allowed is a violation of study permit conditions and can lead to loss of student status, refusal of future permits, and being required to leave Canada.
  • If you are eligible but the work condition is missing from your permit, IRCC can amend it free of charge — but you cannot work, or obtain a Social Insurance Number, until it is added.

Canada's immigration authority has issued a fresh reminder to international students: the right to work is not automatic with a study permit. In a post on X, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada wrote: "You can only work in Canada as an international student if your study permit conditions say you can. If you are eligible to work off campus, you can only work up to 24 hours per week while classes are in session. Working more than you are allowed is a violation of your study permit conditions, which can have serious consequences."

The rule is printed on the permit

IRCC prints one of two conditions on eligible permits, according to the detailed guidance summarised by Immigration.ca: either that the holder may accept employment on or off campus if they meet the eligibility criteria, or that the permit does not authorise off-campus employment and the holder may work only on campus. The permission is not implied by the permit alone. Students also cannot start working before their study programme begins — work that starts even a few days early is unauthorised.

https://x.com/CitImmCanada/status/2116153290513686644

Who qualifies

Off-campus work generally requires full-time enrolment at a designated learning institution in a programme of at least six months leading to a degree, diploma or certificate, a valid study permit carrying the work condition, and a Social Insurance Number. On-campus work — jobs physically on the school's campus — carries no weekly hour limit, but the same permit condition and full-time requirements apply. Since November 2024, students must also be approved for a new study permit before changing designated learning institution.

The consequences of getting it wrong

Exceeding the 24-hour weekly cap during a session is a breach of study permit conditions. IRCC has said it can cost a student their status, lead to refusal of future study or work permits, and require them to leave Canada. The Times of India's report of the reminder, carried by 7Globe, noted the warning followed permit refusals involving Indian students. After graduation, students generally need a work permit; eligible graduates can apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit and, if they meet IRCC's requirements, work full-time while it is processed.

What to check today

Read the conditions section of your study permit before accepting any shift. If the work condition is missing but you meet the criteria, ask IRCC to amend the permit — there is no fee — and wait for the corrected document before starting work.
